title: itembank settings file
description: The one documented settings file, itembank.json, shipped at repository root. Every key is typed, ranged or enumerated, and defaulted here; a key's x-itembank-phase names the phase whose code actually reads it -- a key with no shipped reader yet is still present and settable, but itembank config reports it as inert rather than letting a learner believe it controls behaviour.

theme.description: The app's color theme. Read by this phase (4).

accent.description: The learner's chosen source accent color. Only accent.source is persisted; derived light/dark pairs, contrast ratios, correction notices, and manual per-mode overrides never enter this file (D-05/D-07). Read by this phase (4).

source.description: The learner's chosen source accent as a normalized opaque #RRGGBB hex color. Written only through itembank theme set/pick, which normalize and validate the exact six-digit hex form before persisting; the schema enforces the exact #RRGGBB pattern so a hand-edited file or a config set cannot carry a source the renderer silently ignores.

daily_cap.description: Maximum items served per subject per day. Inert until Phase 10 reads it.

selection_weights.description: Relative weights the item-selection algorithm uses to prioritize which items to serve. Inert until Phase 7 reads it.

objective_miss_rate.description: Weight given to an objective's historical miss rate. Inert until Phase 10's weighting model reads it (TREND-01) -- not this phase's.

difficulty_spread.description: Weight given to spreading served items across difficulty levels. Inert until Phase 10's weighting model reads it (TREND-01) -- not this phase's.

recency_decay.description: The coefficient applied to the recency penalty beyond the hard cooldown window (D-08/D-15): an item's ordering rank is lowered by recency_decay * (1 / (1 + age)) where age is responses since its most recent serving. A value of 0 disables the penalty entirely. Read by phase 7.

cooldown_responses.description: The number of most-recent responses in this bank inside which an item is not re-served (D-08). 0 disables hard exclusion. When every candidate falls inside the window the oldest-seen items are readmitted rather than the session coming back empty. Default 20 (D-08); the starvation case is answered by the readmission rule, not by a smaller number that would weaken the guarantee on a real bank.

profiles.description: User-chosen selection profile names; each value is a selection spec validated against schemas/selection.schema.json when it is used (expand_spec, phase 7). Set a whole map with `itembank config set selection.profiles '{...}'` because a dotted path cannot address a user-chosen key.

auditor_autonomy.description: How much the auditor is allowed to act on its own findings without a human approving each step. Anything beyond report_only is flagged Revisit in PROJECT.md until proven. Inert until Phase 11 reads it.

model_backend.description: Which model backend (if any) the AI-tutoring surfaces call, and where. Inert until Phase 8 reads it.

kind.description: none disables model calls entirely; hosted talks to a network provider; local talks to an OpenAI-compatible server on this machine. Inert until Phase 8 reads it.

endpoint.description: Base URL of the model server; ignored when kind is none. Inert until Phase 8 reads it.

model.description: Model name/identifier passed to the backend; ignored when kind is none. Inert until Phase 8 reads it.

update_policy.description: Whether the opt-in updater checks GitHub Releases automatically. check_on_launch checks once at daemon launch, silently and non-blockingly; opt_in only checks when the user runs itembank update. The declared default is opt_in, so a fresh installation with no settings file makes no automatic check; this repository's own checked-in itembank.json intentionally sets check_on_launch to dogfood the updater (D-13), so the two values are meant to differ. Read by this phase (2.1).

daemon.description: The daemon's own port, LAN, and app-window settings.

port.description: Default port the daemon binds to.

lan.description: Default value for --lan: bind all interfaces so a phone on the same wifi can open it.

open_browser.description: Whether the daemon launches a browser on startup by default.

window.description: Which container the daemon opens its page in: app attempts a frameless Chromium-family --app= window and falls back to an ordinary tab when no such browser is found; tab always opens an ordinary tab. Read by this phase (2.1).

reader.description: The lesson reader's settings (03.1-UI-SPEC section 14). Read by this phase (3.1).

reader_nav.description: Whether the lesson reader shows a sections nav column. none is the locked default; column renders one optional <nav> in the same DOM (03.1-UI-SPEC sections 7.3 and 14).

example_layout.description: How [!EXAMPLE] callouts arrange their steps. stacked is the locked default; parallel is a one CSS-grid class on the same container (03.1-UI-SPEC sections 9.3 and 14).

print_gloss.description: How the gloss prints. appendix is the locked default (the full glossary <dl> prints, popovers hidden); inline un-hides each popover as a small bordered note, first use only (03.1-UI-SPEC sections 10.1 and 14).

gloss_marks.description: How densely [[term]] triggers are marked. all is the locked default; first-use marks only the first occurrence per section; none renders every term as plain prose and leaves the glossary appendix as the only path (03.1-UI-SPEC sections 8.2 and 14).

update.description: Where the opt-in self-updater looks for releases, and how often a background check may run. Read by this phase (2.1).

repo.description: owner/name of the GitHub repository whose Releases the updater reads. A token, when one is used, comes from the ITEMBANK_GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable and never from this file. Read by this phase (2.1).

check_interval_hours.description: Minimum hours between two background update checks, to stay well under GitHub's 60-requests-per-hour unauthenticated limit. Read by this phase (2.1).

style.description: The lesson style system's authoring-prompt and warning-calibration settings (plan 03.1-05, D-14 and D-17). Read by this phase (3.1).

imperative_cap.description: The maximum number of distilled style imperatives the authoring model receives, placed last in the prompt (D-17). Default 7 because the seven-imperative figure is extrapolated from format-compliance research, not measured on pedagogical structure -- a setting so it can be calibrated against the Phase 3.2 corpus without a code change.

warn_fp_threshold.description: The false-positive rate above which a style warning ships disabled by default, with the rate recorded beside the code (D-14). The Phase 3.2 corpus drives the per-code rates; this is the threshold they are measured against.

paraphrase.description: The winnowing paraphrase lint's thresholds (plan 03.2-04, D-13): an item transcribing >= winnow_threshold consecutive words of a source is an error; a fingerprint Jaccard overlap above jaccard_threshold is a warning. Both are settings because they need tuning against the real corpus without a code change. Read by this phase (3.2).

winnow_threshold.description: The number of consecutive copied words that make a paraphrase a transcription (prov.paraphrase_copy, D-13). Default 8.

jaccard_threshold.description: The fingerprint Jaccard overlap above which an item warns for being too close to its source (prov.paraphrase_overlap, D-13). Default 0.25.

retention.description: The retention, pacing and trends thresholds (Phase 10). Every value is bounded here with conservative defaults so later tuning is a settings change, never a code change (D-06, D-23); the weak threshold must stay below the mastery threshold and the weight floor below the ceiling (retention.py rejects contradictory pairs with a named error). Read by this phase (10).

min_settled_attempts.description: Settled outcomes (auto-scored bool, or a constructed response with an accepted human mark) needed before an objective receives a state label at all. Fewer is unknown (D-03).

weak_accuracy.description: Recent settled accuracy below this is the weak state. Must be lower than mastery_accuracy (retention.py rejects equality/inversion with a named error).

mastery_accuracy.description: Recent settled accuracy at or above this, together with mastery_success_days distinct local days of confirmed success, is the mastered state.

mastery_success_days.description: Distinct local days with a confirmed success required for the mastered state.

at_risk_after_days.description: A previously-confirmed-successful objective with no confirming evidence for at least this many days is at-risk (D-14: prior success plus silence, never predicted failure).

review_interval_days.description: The configured objective review interval: a stable objective whose latest settled evidence is at least this old is due (D-04/D-06).

lesson_review_after_days.description: Days after an explicit lesson completion event before its referenced objectives enter the review queue as due (SCHED-04, 10-02).

weight_min.description: Floor of the bounded objective weight multiplier (D-11). Must be below weight_max.

weight_max.description: Ceiling of the bounded objective weight multiplier (D-11). Must be above weight_min.

max_weight_step.description: Maximum absolute change to one objective's normalized weight between snapshots (D-12: gradual, capped, so one bad session cannot cause an extreme next session).

weak_boost.description: Formula term: added to the raw weight of a weak objective (10-RESEARCH.md initial formula).

due_boost.description: Formula term: added to the raw weight of a due objective (10-RESEARCH.md initial formula).

at_risk_boost.description: Formula term: added to the raw weight of an at-risk objective (10-RESEARCH.md initial formula).

mastery_reduction.description: Formula term: subtracted from the raw weight of a mastered objective, keeping it out of ordinary rotation without making it unreachable (D-11).

focused_session_count.description: The bounded size of the focused-session recommendation (D-04).
